diagnosis: Typical lymph node histology in autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS)
legend: Low-power magnification shows reactive follicles with visible germinal centres and well-formed mantle zones; the paracortex is expanded by a pale-staining lymphoid infiltrate, but the overall lymph node architecture is intact (<<30312>>). The interfollicular infiltrate is composed of sheets of pale-staining medium-sized lymphocytes with admixed small lymphocytes, plasma cells, and high endothelial venules (<<30313>>). The medium-sized lymphocytes have irregular nuclear contours and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures are frequent (<<30314>>). The paracortex is expanded by sheets of cytologically atypical lymphocytes with open chromatin, slightly irregular nuclear contours, and visible nucleoli (<<30315>>).

legend: The paracortical expansion is composed of T cells that coexpress CD57 by immunohistochemistry (<<30362>>). Flow immunophenotyping shows a large population of TCRαβ+, CD4−, CD8− T-cell events (<<40319>>).

diagnosis: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS) lymph node with Castleman disease–like changes
legend: Typical Castleman disease–like follicles with regressed germinal centres, onion-skinning, and penetrating small-calibre vessels.

diagnosis: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS) lymph node with Rosai–Dorfman disease
legend: Low-power view of the lymph node reveals irregular eosinophilic foci that stand out against the characteristic paracortical expansion (<<30376>>). The characteristic eosinophilic histiocytes of Rosai–Dorfman disease, notable for their round nuclei and prominent central nucleoli, are admixed with numerous plasma cells (<<30377>>). Emperipolesis, with engulfed lymphocytes and plasma cells within the histiocyte cytoplasm, is evident at high magnification (<<30378>>).

title: Characteristic histological findings and pitfalls of autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS)
tablehtml:
Characteristic histological findings

·      Pale-staining proliferative paracortical DNT cell hyperplasia with plasmacytosis and foci of RDD

·      B-cell follicles with a range of features, from reactive follicular hyperplasia to progressive transformation of germinal centres to Castleman disease–like findings

·      Extranodal sites with mixed lymphoid infiltrates including proliferative DNT cells

Pitfalls

·      Misdiagnosis as peripheral T-cell lymphoma due to cytological atypia, DNT cell phenotype, high Ki-67 index, cytotoxic markers, extranodal infiltrates, occasional γδ T-cell phenotype

·      Masking of underlying ALPS by associated Castleman disease–like findings, RDD, or superimposed IgG4-related disease

·      Increased risk of lymphoma, including some types that may be obscured by a prominent non-neoplastic T-cell component, such as T-cell/histiocyte–rich large B-cell lymphoma and nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma

DNT, CD4/CD8 double-negative T; RDD, Rosai–Dorfman disease.

legend: The lymph node shows paracortical expansion with admixed medium-sized lymphocytes with visible nucleoli and moderate pale-staining cytoplasm and numerous admixed plasma cells. Reactive follicular hyperplasia is present with well-formed mantle zones and polarized germinal centers; a subset of follicles are regressed, with onion-skinning and penetrating vessels.
